title: callhome-silence-hypothesis-lab-notes-2026-10
content:
Summary:

Observed a prolonged callhome silence from multiple on-prem customer control-plane proxies beginning 2026-10-12 03:17 UTC. A subset of private deployments stopped emitting health pings to the control plane; this manifested as UI gaps in Console, missing traces in control-plane logs, and stalled config push attempts. No customer workloads were reported 'down' by the app owners but autoscaling and policy updates failed to apply.

Why this doc exists:
- Working notes from initial triage and lab reproduction attempts.
- Hypotheses, quick experiments run in lab, and next-runbook candidates.
- Keep shortest possible checklist for oncall to triage callhome silence in the future.

High-level impact:
- Affected: ~12 tenants across two on-prem clusters (region: eu-west-1-sbx equivalents).
- Symptoms: control-plane-heartbeat missing, connection counts drop to near-zero, local telemetry shows normal app traffic.
- Duration: ~03:17 UTC -> 04:02 UTC (~45 minutes) for the earliest cluster; other clusters saw intermittent recovery.

Observed signals (raw):
- Control-plane metrics: CONN_ESTABLISHED_PER_PROXY dropped 98% at 03:18 UTC.
- Proxy logs: repeated 5xx on health-check end -> "TLS handshake aborted" (see excerpt below).
- Customer onprem firewall telemetry: bursts of SYN retries to control-plane IPs starting 03:16 UTC.
- Snippets from proxy logs: "callhome-client: write: broken pipe"; "callhome: upstream reset while sending".

Timeline (key events):
- 03:12 UTC: scheduled kc-sync job ran (internal config job).
- 03:16 UTC: first spike in SYN retries recorded by customer edge FW.
- 03:17 UTC: callhomes start dropping; control-plane dashboards show missing heartbeats.
- 03:22 UTC: SRE oncall (Asha) opens SRE-4821, posts to #oncall-private-deployments.
- 03:27 UTC: temporary mitigation applied (increase TCP retries on proxy side, see mitigations).
- 03:38 UTC: partial recovery observed for cluster A; clusters B/C oscillated.
- 04:02 UTC: most proxies reestablished; root cause not confirmed.

Initial hypotheses tested:
1) Customer firewall policy started dropping long-lived outbound control connections due to conntrack or DPI thresholding.
   - Evidence for: FW telemetry shows SYN retries, and some TCP RSTs with reason "conn-limit" in vendor logs.
   - Against: Not all customers show matching FW alerts; when we asked two customers they had no policy changes at that time.

2) On-prem proxy TLS renegotiation bug triggered by our control-plane switching to a new cert chain at 03:15.
   - Evidence for: We rotated an intermediate cert in a routine job at 03:10 (internal ticket GH PR#2143). Some proxies logged "TLS alert: bad certificate".
   - Against: Several proxies continued to accept other TLS sessions; handshake failures are only in callhome channel.

3) Kernel-level ephemeral port exhaustion or conntrack table saturation on customer CPE devices causing L7 devices to drop established flows (callhome uses long TCP keepalive).
   - Evidence for: Packet captures from customer environment show FIN/RESET patterns and long retransmit sequences.
   - Against: No system-level conntrack overflow counters visible on all hosts (limited telemetry).

Lab reproduction attempts (notes):
- Lab setup: created 3-node onprem proxy cluster (vm: proxy-a/b/c), a simulated customer firewall (pfSense VM with conntrack limits), and a control-plane stub server that accepts callhome connections and responds to heartbeats.

Experiment A: Reduce conntrack table size on pfSense to 1024 and run 1500 outbound connections from proxies with 120s keepalive.
- Result: conntrack overflowed after ~2 minutes; pfSense started dropping established connections, observed SYN retries and RSTs.
- Reproduced similar log lines seen in customer telemetry.

Experiment B: Re-deploy with same setup but trigger an intermediate cert rotation on control-plane while connections established.
- Result: observed intermittent TLS handshake aborts but not full-scale silence; ~10% of sessions reset but majority rehandshook.

Experiment C: Simulate DPI/idle-flow timeout by enabling aggressive TCP reaper that kills flows older than 30s.
- Result: Long-lived callhome flows were killed; control-plane saw connection churn; local proxies attempted reconnects with exponential backoff and eventually recovered.

Synthesis of lab work:
- Most reproducible match to customer telemetry was conntrack exhaustion / aggressive middlebox that drops established connections under resource pressure.
- Cert rotation may have amplified the issue in some environments (handshake aborts cause reconnect storms which push middlebox counters).

Temporary mitigations applied during incident:
- Increase client-side reconnect jitter and cap reconnect rate (reduce thundering-herd effect). Applied as a hotfix to callhome client config (rollback-able).
- Increase TCP retransmit attempts and adjust keepalive to 60s for the callhome channel to reduce perceived connection drops.
- Ask impacted customers to check CPE conntrack and increase table sizes for the maintenance window (customer ops).

Runbook changes proposed (short list for next PR):
1) New triage section: "Callhome silence - middlebox/backpressure checklist"
   - Check FW conntrack counters, DPI logs, NAT translation table sizes, and vendor-specific alerts.
2) Pre-deploy checklist for scheduled cert rotations: include a canary group and staggered rollouts with monitoring for callhome churn metrics.
3) Add a small script to control-plane console to show per-proxy last-heartbeat + client TLS error histogram to speed root-cause pinning.
4) Default client config change: enable reconnect-jitter and max-reconnect-rate in shipped onprem proxy by default (opt-out via local config).

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Asha: draft runbook PR for callhome-silence checklist (ETA: 2026-10-18).
- Diego: add heartbeat+tls histogram endpoint to control-plane metrics (ETA: 2026-10-22).
- Priya: reach out to top-3 impacted customers to request conntrack dump and vendors' support case numbers (ETA: 2026-10-14).
- Evan: capture a reproducible pcap and annotate with packet-level timeline for GH PR#2143 (ETA: 2026-10-16).

Quick triage checklist for oncall (2-min run through):
1) Check control-plane: heartbeat_missing > 5m? Check per-proxy last_seen.
2) If last_seen gap correlates across multiple proxies in same tenant: ask customer to check edge FW conntrack, NAT mappings, and DPI events.
3) Check if we deployed certs or rolled jobs in previous 30m (look at GH PRs & deploy timeline).
4) If customer reports normal app traffic but callhome silent: suspect middlebox; request tcpdump of outbound traffic from proxy to control-plane.
5) Apply hotfix (reconnect-jitter) if reconnect storms likely; coordinate with product for hotfix rollout.

Notes to self / unresolved questions:
- Need to capture more vendor-specific conntrack names and where to look across common customer appliances (Cisco ASA, Palo Alto, Fortigate, pfSense).
- Should we consider shifting callhome to use QUIC (UDP) opportunistically? That changes middlebox behavior but has different NAT traversal characteristics. Worth R&D.
- How to measure "silent drop" vs. "early TCP close" more reliably without asking customer pcaps? Could we add a small UDP-based probe as secondary telemetry?

Appendix A: Useful commands and log snippets
- control-plane metrics quick query:
  sum by(proxy) (increase(control_plane_heartbeat_total[5m]))

- proxy-side quick check (on onprem proxy host):
  sudo ss -tanp | grep <control-plane-ip>
  sudo conntrack -S | egrep 'entries|found'   # vendor-dependent

- sample proxy log lines (redacted):
  Oct 12 03:17:48 proxy-a callhome-client[2143]: WARN callhome: write failed: broken pipe
  Oct 12 03:18:02 proxy-a callhome-client[2143]: WARN callhome: TLS handshake aborted: bad certificate

Appendix B: Lab artifacts
- pcap: lab/pcaps/callhome_conntrack_overflow.pcap (attached to GH PR#2143)
- experiment notes: lab/exp-notes/conntrack-overflow-1024.txt

If you are reading this during an active incident: use the quick triage checklist above first, escalate to SRE lead if >2 tenants affected or cross-region impact.

-- Asha

"Notes to future me: document vendor-specific conntrack counters and add them to the runbook. And schedule a 1-hour war room to validate the hotfix behavior with a partner customer next month."
